topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, instructor introduction, and learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer fundamentals, mutation sources, and genetic predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the basic nature of cancer as a genetic and microenvironmental disease driven by endogenous mutations, cellular replication stress, and inherited predispositions.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens, epidemiology, and the 'bad luck' debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore environmental exposures, public perception surrounding stochastic 'bad luck' versus preventable risk, and epidemiological evidence showing geographic variation in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents and pathogen-driven carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how oncogenic pathogens, including bacteria, parasites, and viruses, contribute to malignancy, illustrated by the mechanism and geography of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical, physical, and promoter-driven carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical radiation, dietary toxins, xenobiotic metabolic activation, tumor promotion pathways, and developmental susceptibility windows cause and facilitate carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for detecting, testing, and evaluating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine carcinogenicity and assess human exposure risks.

topics.label: Conclusion and final summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing and final summary of the lecture.
